cells.tense: You are standing at the far side of an imagining that has become real enough to feel.
cells.ask: Take the one you have been circling and make it concrete for someone today: put it where they can see it, in a form they can hold.
cells.core: Something you imagined long enough and felt deeply enough has arrived at the far side of the imagining, and the satisfaction is real. You can see the whole pattern of it — how the pieces came, what they add up to now. That is a good place to stand, holding a larger picture in view while staying inside it. It isn't perfect, and it doesn't have to be. Being satisfied with what was imagined feels unusual, like standing somewhere you aren't supposed to stay. You are free to keep what arrived, to choose the imagined life and live inside it rather than walk away from it. What comes next doesn't have to be a demand; it can be something quiet, done because it fits and feels true.
cells.sheetLine: What was imagined has arrived, and you can feel it.
cells.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
cells.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.

cells.tense: You are bracing in front of a life that still has to be made proof, so the imagining is running ahead of what has actually happened.
cells.ask: Pick one seed and tend it this week — the same one — and let that be the whole of the striving, nothing extra.
cells.core: You keep trying to hold the whole pattern steady, and your grip is going past what one hand can carry. Every version of the future gets sorted, compared, held up against the next version before any of it has had time to grow. The largeness you are waiting for hasn't arrived, and you are treating that as a problem you can force into shape. Some of what you want is already in front of you in a smaller form; it is being passed over. Care that clutches takes energy and gives panic back. The way through isn't a bigger plan. It is one plant you actually water. Keep it small enough to hold, and let the rest wait.
cells.sheetLine: The life you want cannot be built by forcing the timing.
cells.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
cells.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.

cells.tense: You are still facing a door you once imagined opening, standing in front of it even though it closed behind you.
cells.ask: Write down one word that feels true today, without judging it, and read it again tonight.
cells.core: The imagining is still going on somewhere, but it stopped coming through to the present. You can see pieces of what might be true, the shape of it, and nothing lands anywhere or chooses. So nothing has arrived, and the whole picture stays out of reach. There isn't much fuel for this right now, and pushing harder only makes the quiet louder. What charges it is smaller. One honest word, kept to yourself for a while, proves more than a large conclusion forced out too soon. Trusting you can be sure of things without announcing them keeps the imagining from becoming a promise you rush to keep. Pick one thing to know quietly.
cells.sheetLine: It is safe to know what you know before you say it.
cells.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
cells.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.

cells.tense: You are already making the life you imagined, and you tell the story as if it arrived on its own.
cells.ask: Name one thing you made that you call luck or timing, and say you did it. Do it once, out loud.
cells.core: The imagining has been going on the whole time — and it has been yours. The choices that grew into this were made by you, one at a time, and the whole pattern only holds together because you kept working it. What gets said is that things just happened, or the moment was right, or someone else set it up. The making is still going; it hasn't stopped. The credit is sitting right next to the work, waiting. Once you take one piece of it in your own hand, the whole picture sharpens, because it finally has an author. You can see the pattern without needing it to have been given to you.
cells.sheetLine: The life you wanted is one you made.
cells.verb: Imagining a life of your own and feeling it through until the first full yes, the one experience cannot take back.
cells.place: Standing far enough back to see the whole pattern, still inside it.

attempts.check: My draft invents a mechanism — that the loop of sorting and comparing is specifically what keeps anything from satisfying — where the record only names abundance felt as the place satisfaction appears, and it risks sounding like an instruction to stop examining things. The reader could reasonably say I don't do that, my doubt isn't the problem, and the ask would still stand because it is only a choosing act, not a repair for a bad quality. The sentence that serves me more than them was the reflex to explain the blessing, as if I were owed the reason everything arrived; the plain description is enough.
